items.text: It’s been about a month since Towerborne 1.0 released, and during that time we’ve been working on a patch to fix many of the issues we’ve seen reported, including players affected by modified Scale display settings.

The Skill Point cost of Light Focus Skills and Heavy Focus Skills have been universalized across all classes:
Light Focus Skills = 3 SP
Heavy Focus Skills = 4 SP
Jackhammer changed from 5 SP -> 4 SP
Crownbreaker changed from 5 SP -> 4 SP
Silver Strikes changed from 5 SP -> 4 SP

Fixed an issue that prevented dodging after performing a Dash Heavy Attack (dropkick)
You can now dodgeroll in all directions when laying on the ground
Pro Tip: Equip the Heavy Rolling Attack Skill to really take advantage of this ability!
Fixed an issue where Dash Heavy Attack (dropkick) did not cause the correct hit reaction on enemies that were laying on the ground
This now knocks enemies away and has more oomph

Pyro Surge

Fixed an issue that caused many heavy attacks and Weapon Mechanic Skills to get interrupted by enemy attacks too early
Improved the general comboability of basic attacks so that it’s easier to juggle airborne enemies more consistently
Fixed an issue where Weapon Meter gain from incoming attacks was incorrect when using the Thermal Amplification Skill

items.text: This Launch Overview is meant to give all players a clear, high‑level insight into what Towerborne 1.0 is today.

If you’re returning from Early Access, we’ve also written a Letter to Early Access Players that highlights key areas we expanded and improved based on your feedback. You can read both, or jump straight to the letter if you’re looking for those details.
A New Beginning
Select your class at creation and change it freely between missions as you refine your playstyle
Experience the fall of the City of Numbers firsthand, battling to protect its people
Come face to face with the event that forges you into a deathless Ace, guardian of the last remnants of humanity
A New World
Experience a 15+ hour campaign to protect the Belfry, discover the machinations that led to the fall of Numbers, and fight alongside fellow Aces to set the world right
Freely explore the map to advance the campaign, aid refugees, and discover new allies
Throughout the campaign, NPC companions will join you on select missions, expanding the story and lore while fighting alongside you against the horde
Each companion brings player‑like combat abilities, capable of extending combos, setting up juggles, and helping you overcome some of the toughest challenges
Your Danger Level increases as you progress, peeling back the fog of war, revealing new environments, and bringing you closer to the City of Numbers
All campaign missions are through the World Map or Quest menu
Bounty Board
Sharpen your skills and test your limits through the Bounty Board located on the Belfry
Battle though 100 missions with custom scenarios, including unique versions of lieutenants and bosses
Earn Gear, Umbra and Skills by completing specific challenges
Face new variant bosses, Trials, Courage Crucibles and Krafft’s Gauntlets for repeatable rewards that scale with the challenge
Complete the campaign to unlock additional Bounties designed to test all your skills and your build
Endlessly Versatile Combat
Combat in Towerborne is fast, fluid, and expressive, built around mobility, choice, and customization
Engage in highly mobile combat with 8‑way dodges and rolls, multiple combo paths, and distinct combo enders that offer different utility
Player expression is at the core of Towerborne’s combat, progression, and upgrade systems, letting you shape how you fight and grow
Classes & Mastery
Choose from four distinct Classes, each with deep, expansive movesets
Version 1.0 introduces new and refined Class Mastery skills, along with Universal skills that, once unlocked, are available across all classes
Freely redistribute skill points at any time to refine your build or experiment with new approaches
Umbra
Ally with an Umbra and use its unique ability to turn the tide of battle
New Umbra have been added bringing with them unique mechanics new to Towerborne
Find new aspects that modify the behavior of Umbra abilities
Gear
Complete Ventures to earn Gear Sets, unlocking additional bonuses when enough pieces are equipped
Defeat bosses to earn weapons with new and unique perks
Discover legendary weapons and gear as you progress deeper into the world, and challenge the Bounty Board for new Boss Legendary weapons
Mix and match to freely equip multiple gear sets, stack legendaries, and experiment without restriction
Further customize your Helm, Chest, and Weapon items with Aspects that grant new perks and stats
Perfect your gear with the Forge
Upgrade gear Spirit Dust to increase attack and defense
Fuse unwanted gear to make new gear, giving you more control over what you earn
Reforge to change unwanted stats tailor items to your needs
Refine stats on gear to maximize their values and perfect your loadout
All Cosmetics, Your Way, It’s All About the Look
All cosmetic items are earned through gameplay through mission rewards, the Writs Store, and Curios
No microtransactions. Unlockable Cosmetics are acquired with Writs, a currency earned by playing
Everything from Early Access is included, along with 50+ brand‑new armor sets and tons of new weapon skins making 1.0 the ultimate cosmetic collection
Early Access players will have all cosmetics they have already acquired during the Early Access period
Style any gear you find. Create cosmetic versions of any dropped gear, including Legendaries, using Writs, so you’re never locked into a look
More play = more Writs
As you progress through the Campaign and take on Bounty Board missions, you’ll unlock additional ways to earn Writs and increase your rewards
Play Your Way
Danger Levels & Progression
The world of Towerborne grows more dangerous the deeper you go. Help Paloma keep the Belfry safe to increase your Danger Level, accessing new areas and encounters
Rise to the challenge by earning levels, unlocking new skills, and earning more powerful gear
Flexible Difficulty
Whether you’re new to action brawlers or a battle‑hardened champion, Towerborne lets you choose how challenging the fight should be.
Difficulty can be adjusted at any time from the mission selection screen
Higher difficulties reward additional Writs and Spirit Dust, allowing you to further customize your appearance and gear
Level Sync
Jumping into missions below your current level automatically enables Level Sync, making it easy to play with friends at different stages of the game
Your stats scale down so you still feel powerful without overwhelming the mission
Earn gear you usable for your current level, regardless of the mission’s Danger Level
Disable Level Sync to overpower earlier missions and earn gear at the mission’s Danger Level, perfect for jump-starting a new class
Save Slots & Replayability
Towerborne includes 4 save slots
Early Access players retain access to their curio progress, cosmetic purchases, Writs, and Stepstones

Or start a fresh save and still maintain all curio progress, cosmetic purchases, and Writs
Once Brutal difficulty is unlocked, start a new save and test your build mastery, combat skill, and decision making from the first fight to the final victory
Reset save slots anytime if you want a clean run
Take Towerborne on the road with offline play
Play With Friends
Towerborne is built to be played together—online or on the couch.
Online Co Op (Same Platform)
Play with up to 4 players online, each with their own gameplay camera, making it easier to coordinate and tackle larger encounters
Couch Co Op (Xbox Series S|X & PlayStation 5)
Play locally with up to 4 players on a shared screen and a single camera. It’s a more coordinated experience that rewards teamwork and positioning
Host Driven Adventure
When playing in a group, the host drives progression, pulling friends into missions and deeper challenges
This makes it easy to jump in together and keep the adventure moving forward
Scaling & Level Sync
Difficulty scales with party size to keep encounters engaging Level Sync ensures that players can have fun with newer friends without overwhelming the experience
Want More Challenge?

On Hard and Brutal, Elite enemies have a chance to become Vanguards, dangerous leaders that empower nearby foes
Spot the Vanguard and eliminate the threat to cancel enemy buffs
Fallen Vanguards drop a pickup that grants temporary buff yourself and your party, turning the tide in your favor.
Starting a new save and conquering Brutal from the beginning is where this mode truly shines:
Enemies use the most aggressive AI behaviors, with expanded kits and surprises (watch out for cluster bombs)
Harder hits, tougher fights, and more demanding environments including new enemy spawners and hazard scenarios

In addition to a suite of class, combat, and enemy tweaks, we’ve got some new things for you to try in this update—starting with a brand-new system we’re calling Community Requests, plus a major refresh to how you earn Writs throughout the game.

New Feature! Community Requests: Community Requests are now live! These time-limited challenges invite all Aces to contribute toward a shared goal. Each request includes personal objectives for you to tackle on your own, plus large-scale Belfry-wide milestones.

You’ll find Community Requests in the Request Board in the Tower under the new Community tab. The first event, Rakentague Overflow, focuses on Grasslands missions, Beastkin, and Bloodletters … more detail below!

Writ Reward Updates: We’ve fine-tuned how Writs are earned across early missions and the Job Board to help smooth out the path for new and returning Aces. More on Writs and in-game economy soon ... for now, here's what you can expect with this update.
For rookie Aces just stepping into Towerborne, the early game grind has been lightened to get you moving faster.
Several early missions now reward 400 Writs (up from 250)
Job Board tasks now scale from 80 to 160 Writs based on difficulty.
Requests have also been made more flexible—no need to hunt down one exact Venture anymore; now you can take on any Venture and still make progress.
The Bell questline has been refreshed - complete it again to earn extra Writs.
Check out update details, below.
Community Request: Rakentague Overflow
A tide of enemies is coming from the Rakentague area. The Council has deemed this threat to be Ace Level, and bounties are issued. Help protect the refugees in the area!

Community Requests are a new feature added to Towerborne in this update. This is a 3 week challenge. Each step unlocks automatically after the step before it is completed. Work together as a Community to complete the new Request to claim rewards!
Ace Goals
Complete 5 missions in Grasslands
Defeat 200 Beastkin
Complete the Rakentague Venture
Belfry Goals
Complete 1000 missions in Grasslands
Defeat 10000 Beastkin
Defeat 1000 Ratslasher Bloodletters

Community Requests can be found in the Request Board located in the Tower. Tab over to the Community section to see the new additions to the board. Rewards can be claimed at the board (for each step). At the end of the event, you’ll be sent unclaimed rewards automatically via in-game mail.

[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/25a69c519461beb2773d930548c3baf5359983d3.png"]Greetings, Aces!

From the moment Towerborne hit Early Access last September—and through April’s game-shaping update—you’ve been with us every swing of the Warclub. You’ve toppled titans, lit up Umbra Shrines, leveled classes, and traded war stories in the Belfry. We set out to build a game we wanted to play, and we knew it would only reach its full potential with you right beside us.

That spirit fuels our latest (massive) update-celebration, Echoes of Gratitude. From bug-hunting to every “hey, what if…?” our Founders - those Aces who've played with us on our road to 1.0 launch - have helped sculpted Towerborne into what it is today, and like any good squad-mate, we've got your back!

With this update, expect a bigger world and a deeper game, including a new Danger Level 5 zone, new Ventures, new Chance Encounters, new enemies and a new Umbra - and more. Quality of life improvements include early runs feeling smoother, fewer pop-ups, a rebalanced DL 2 trial, cleaner mission flow, and more.

To show our thanks, we’re throwing the Belfry doors wide open for a week of Free Play Days! Yes, it’s exactly like it sounds … play for free on Steam (June 11–18) or Xbox (June 12–18) - these Free Play Days serve two purposes: first, a big thank-you! And second, they’ll help us test our systems to make sure we ship the best possible game when we officially launch - for everyone! Beyond that, we’ve lined up a slate of in game (and out-of-game) goodies – see the full list below!
Give it all a whirl and - as always - we can’t wait to hear what you think.
We hope all of what we’ve got in store resonates with you - each item below is a version of our way of saying - thank you for suiting up alongside us!

Introducing the Class Skills Progression System! As you level up your Class, unlock a huge variety of Skills across 5 categories: Focus Skills, Weapon Mechanic, Moveset, Advanced Combat, and Support. The Class Skills system adds a whole new world of possibilities to each Class. It’s up to you to pick and choose your Skills in a way that best suits your playstyle.
Class Skills Progression System

One of the biggest changes to combat comes in the form of Class Skills. This new progression mechanic aims to provide players with a large variety of choice and customization options that unlock as you level up your Classes.

Each Skill has a Skill Point Cost associated with it. However, spending points is not a permanent action. You are able to Equip or Unequip Skills however you like, provided you have enough points to do so. There are five main categories to customize: Focus Skills, Weapon Mechanic, Moveset, Advanced Combat, and Support.
New! The Mender’s Flask

The concept of Lives has been removed from the game. It is now replaced by the Mender’s Flask. Pressing Up on the d-pad will allow the Ace to heal 40% of your health. In solo play, reaching zero health will now result in Defeat.
It will be possible to improve various aspects of Healing as you progress through the game.

Focus Skills are no longer locked to specific weapons. Instead, Focus Skills are unlocked via leveling up the Class of your choice. This means it’s now possible to mix and match your favorite Light and Heavy Focus Skills!

Weapon Mechanics have been greatly expanded thanks to the new Skill system. Some of the new Skills provide small tweaks or improvements to existing mechanics, while others provide all new opportunities that drastically change the way you play.
The Ace’s Standard Moveset can also be expanded with new Skills. You’ll be able to perform air evades, recover quickly when launched, or even perform wake up attacks after being knocked down.
Advanced Combat is where you add new moves, modify existing moves, or apply unique perks to your Class. Some of these are pretty wild, so please look forward to checking them all out!

The Support category is where you can modify your Class to do things that help you when times are tough. Need more Mender’s Flasks? Want to help heal your party? Want to survive a devastating attack that normally would lead to defeat?

Happy 2025! Our first update of the year is here—bringing exciting new updates, including mission types and map improvements, expanded language support, and a special perk for Founders: the ability to claim all previous Monthly Bonuses.

Kicking things off, the World Map will feature three new mission types. Each can be completed once, and some have graduated from discovery tiles to permanent spots on the map. Beyond that, we’ve fine-tuned combat and enemy behaviors, and polished up the visuals (no more NPCs mysteriously losing their faces—oops!). Enemies now have sharper responses and clearer tells, making fights challenging but fair. Plus, this update brings some love to your inventory, tweaks to item stats, and improved mission flow to keep things moving.
What’s that you say? More-monster-mangling was your New Year’s Resolution, too?! Well, then—what are you waiting for? Ready up, Aces … this year is gonna be a doozy.

items.text: ...and all through the Tower,
Fellow Aces were stirring—hey, there’s loot to be scoured!
... for Umbra were nestled in hues rainbow-bright,
While mistle torches burned softly, lighting up the night.
Bumble was quiet, his thoughts far away,
Ogden had plans to bring joy to the day.
“Take him to the mountains!” he said with a grin,
“To witness the light shows and let Yuletide begin!”
With Aces prepared and Bumble in tow,
Through snow-covered trails, they braved the wild glow.
To a bonfire of mistle they traveled with care,
A gift from their friends—a spark to repair.
High in the north, where the skies softly gleam,
Bundles are burned, inspired by a dream.
From mistle trees' branches and secretive lore,
Families create hues that light up the shore.
But beware, brave Aces, for Gobos abound,
They’ve swapped bombs for brass bells with a jingling sound.
Don’t be fooled—yes, their chimes may delight,
Get close, and BOOM—it’ll end your good night!
As furnaces roar and the Belfry stands tall,
The season of Grandeur brings warmth to us all.
Gather your allies, your quest is near—
‘Tis the season to conquer this festive frontier!
Season’s Greetings, Aces!
With this update, we’re thrilled to unveil Towerborne’s December Update, Grandeur, decking the tower-halls with a wave of holiday magic!

Enjoy the Belfry adorned with festive decorations while you embark on a delightful quest to help Bumble rekindle his holiday spirit. Don’t forget to partake in the “12 Days of Grandeur” for daily sticker surprises. Plus, we’re excited to announce localization—Towerborne now supports 18 total languages to spread the love (and punching/stabbing/slicing/bludgeoning).

As we continue our Early Access journey, Founder feedback remains essential in shaping Towerborne into something truly special. So please, keep the feedback coming! And in the meantime, jump into Grandeur and celebrate this festive season with us!
Here's what to expect...

notes.title: Calling All Aces … From Around the World!

items.text: As winter winds swirl and festive lights glow in every corner, Towerborne is proudly throwing its doors open to adventurers far and wide. What’s the best gift we could give this season? A chance for more heroes, from more places, to join the party!

Beyond English, you can now immerse yourself in heroic quests, playful banter, and rich storytelling in French, Italian, Latin American Spanish, Castilian Spanish, German, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Portuguese, Russian, Hungarian, Czech, Dutch, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, and Greek. Each language adds its own spark, uniting us beneath one tower, one banner, and one grand adventure.

And we’re just getting started! As we march ever closer to our full release, expect even more languages and greater global accessibility. Together, we’re forging a worldwide community of heroes—because the only thing better than slaying monsters and snagging epic loot is doing it side by side, no matter where you call home. Your voice, your language, your adventure—let’s take on the world together!

Experience the Belfry adorned with holiday-themed décor: rainbow smoke swirls from the Forge, gift boxes are tucked around every corner, and everyone’s rocking their best festive outfits. Even your Umbra buddies are sporting adorable holiday looks. It’s the perfect setting for seasonal adventures—whether it be lighting Mistle Torches or battling frustrating festive foes like Gobos tossing brass bell bombs and cold-hearted Snow Howlers.

This update’s special, heartwarming quest will have you helping our favorite Forge overseer rekindle his holiday spirit. Accompany Bumble as you take a trip to the mountains—braving the rugged terrain and dodging brass bell bombs along the way. It’s times like these that the most fruitful festive-filled friendships are, well, forged.

To start your Grandeur adventure, make sure you’ve completed the primary quest, “A Writ of Passage.” Then, head to Ogden in The Belfry at the Counsel Building to pick up the next quest, “A Grand Plan.”

What’s holiday cheer without some holiday gear? Get ready for a festive arsenal of gear sets, and weapons sure to send wintery shivers down those monster spines. Here's a sneak peek at what's in store, with the full list of details in notes below.

Join the “12 Days of Grandeur” and collect a daily surprise. Each day presents a new sticker to showcase your festive spirit in-game, adding a playful and creative touch to your character’s appearance. There are 12 stickers in all—check out a teaser of our first sticker below!

Towerborne now speaks your language—literally! From the buzzing streets of Berlin to the snowy peaks of the Alps … from Tokyo’s neon nights to the bustling markets of São Paulo … and a whole bunch of places in between—we’re welcoming Aces to suit up from all over the world.

Play in 18 languages, including English, French, Italian, Latin American Spanish, Castilian Spanish, German, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Portuguese, Russian, Hungarian, Czech, Dutch, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, and Greek. The Belfry is becoming a multi-lingual party—so pick your language, grab your controller/keyboard, and join a global adventure!
To select a preferred language, you have to change language directly within Towerborne’s in-game settings. Steam language settings do not carry over to the game.
1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Language.
2. Scroll through the language options using the left or right arrow.
3. Confirm your selection when prompted.

From a festive new questline that sends you to snowy peaks to improved loot rewards, handy new settings, and even a quick return to the Belfry, there’s something for every adventurer this season. Over the last few months, combat has steadily sharpened with each new update—attacks are snappier, evades flow smoother, and Classes have gained a few slick moves. In this update, we’re thrilled to introduce universal Jump Cancels, no longer limited to specific attacks! This long-awaited change clears old hurdles and opens a whole new realm of combos and strategies. While we’ll keep tweaking it over time, Jump Cancels are already in a great place. So dive in, leap into action, and enjoy the newfound freedom as you carve your path to victory!

Just over two months ago, Towerborne entered Steam Early Access with 40+ hours of core gameplay, a collection of classes to conquer, gobs of gear to grind for, and bands of baddies blundering between biomes—begging to be beaten down.
Today, we’re thrilled to roll out our biggest gameplay update during early access.

We are raising the stakes with the heightened challenge of Danger Level 5—which brings dozens upon dozens more hours of gameplay that can stack up fast (depending on where you’re at in your journey and, let’s be real, just how much loot you’ve stashed). Speaking of loot, more mastery means better gear—we’re introducing the first batch of Legendary items for players to discover alongside an expanded world with over 100 new map tiles waiting to be explored.

We cherish the connection that we share with our players—and inviting all of you Founders to join us on this journey is how we keep building towards the future we talked about when we started Early Access. Of course, don’t forget that we absolutely love to show our appreciation to all of you as we continue doling out sweet Founder Bonus gear … because who doesn't love fighting and frolicking while flashing fresh Founder gear? Nobody, that's who!

We are only a couple of months into Early Access and we’ve been hard at work updating the game, and you can expect that in the weeks and months to come, we will continue this trend: Releasing new updates, sharing more information about what we're working on, and continuing to listen to your feedback. For now, know that Towerborne will keep evolving with said feedback from our Founders, forging the way forward. We’re beyond grateful to be on this journey with you and can’t wait to hear what you think about Danger Level 5 and everything that comes with it!

items.text: NEW Group Finder (V1) ➔ We've heard your feedback on the woes of matchmaking and are introducing an early version of a Group Finder. It’s not fully functional yet - but we wanted to get something in your hands ASAP that we can build on over the coming months.
NEW Danger Level 5 ➔ Our first big content drop, expanding the map, raising the level cap to 50, and introducing tougher enemies to challenge seasoned Aces.
NEW Boss Fight: The Triumverate Awaits ➔ If you thought that Pangojira and Yxil were a threat, wait until you see what's waiting for you in the Heart of Numbers…
NEW Ventures ➔ Embark on four additional Ventures packed with formidable foes and exclusive rewards.
NEW Legendary Weapons and Gear ➔ Discover Legendary items with unique perks, adding custom power and depth to your loadout.
NEW Umbra ➔ Encounter new Umbra companions with unique abilities to aid and amplify your adventures.
Here's a summary of the most exciting pieces of this big update. For more details, check out the section that follows.

The first iteration of the Group Finder is here to help connect Aces for multiple missions and varied gameplay experiences. Group leaders can advertise their groups, and players can find and automatically join groups that match their preferences. Please note that this is an early release of the Group Finder and is NOT considered FEATURE COMPLETE.

How does it work? In this first iteration of the Group Finder, we are still attempting to automatically match players together, but we've dramatically reduced the total number of pools to find people. Now, instead of waiting for more players to join you on a specific tile, you can form up a Group on the Belfry and head out to play as you wish.

Location and Danger Level options help streamline initial connections. Locations include "Any" or "Venture Farming," while Danger Levels are split into "Any," "1-3" and "4-5" to help Aces connect faster with compatible groups.
If a group is set to "Any," it will only match with other players or groups set to "Any." If a player is searching with "Any," they can match with any available group.
Players will need to remain on the Belfry while using Group Finder.
Group leaders can cancel the search at any time and start an adventure with an incomplete group if they choose.

How Is Group Finder Improving matchmaking?THIS IS JUST THE START! We needed to get this feature in your hands as quickly as possible. From here we will add more options, including the ability to see a list of groups and select the one you would like to join. Expect us to significantly increase the support of this feature over the coming months. As we expand, we plan to add options like switching between the Map and Belfry while using Group Finder and seeing a list of groups currently searching for Aces.

How can you help us? Let us know what you're using Group Finder for in the comments here on Steam, or over on Discord. Your feedback will help us determine what additional settings groups need going forward.
The new Danger License Trial unlocks Danger Level 5 - which includes:
Raising the level cap to 50 for a more challenging experience.
4 New Legendary Weapons, one for each class, each weapon features unique perks that add powerful options to your combat style.
12 New Legendary Gear Items: Players can equip up to 2 Legendary gear items and one legendary weapon at the same time. Legendary items will show up only at DL5.

A new chapter unfolds with the Mystweavers, bringing a fierce new battle deep within the Heart of Numbers. Prepare to face this mysterious new boss challenge by completing Ventures in DL3, DL4, and DL5.

Explore more of Towerborne with an expanded world map that includes new Discovery Missions, new Ventures, new loot, new foes, and new Umbra companions exclusive to Danger Level 5. Four new Ventures await:
Numbers Ironworks: Mystweavers have taken over this industrial zone.
Silver-Gold Gates: Beastkin now control the district, preventing access.
Garrison: The Merks occupy this fort—are they working with the Mystweavers?
Heart of Numbers: The site of the City of Numbers explosion, now hosting the ultimate Mystweaver challenge.
Two new missions introduce fresh challenges and unique Umbra allies who have joined us after emerging from the mysterious depths of the Ebb...
The wise and calculating Picus has spent years navigating the veil between the Shore and Ebb; this metallic is known to be a skilled navigator adept at guiding Aces through hazardous terrain...

...or team up with Grimel – steadfast and studious, Grimel delights in lighting up dark areas and helping people look for missing items. They enjoy the smell of parchment to the point that some may find the pages of new books to be irresistibly tasty.

Our Danger Level 5 Update brings continued balance adjustments that refine core gameplay as new content arrives. This update introduces improvements to gear, Umbra companions, and enemies, ensuring a cohesive experience. Healing Shrines now cleanse status effects, adding a strategic edge, while expanded Aspect storage, clearer mission banners, and an optimized Forge layout make inventory and UI management smoother than ever.

Hey all, NotReallyAJedi here, I wanted to drop in and give a quick update on the promised roadmap. This one is 100% on me and I’m sorry we haven’t posted one. I know it sounds a bit cliche, but it’s been crazy since we’ve released and our primary focus has been getting things fixed, updated, created, and released for you. When it comes to remapping your controls - you asked, so you shall receive!
Just a day into our first sizable update and we're pushing a few more fixes and improvements your way… and - by popular demand - you can now customize your key bindings, keyboard players.
Concisely conveyed, we crafted a core capability called upon by our committed community keen on conquering critical combos courtesy of customizable controls (say that five times fast!).
We heard you loud and clear: you want to punch / slash / stab / club through the Wilds in your own way …

It turns out that implementing control remapping is a bit bigger than initially anticipated. Right now, the full implementation of control remapping will take awhile as we work to get the UI elements in place, but the core functionality of remapping is available. So we pulled forward custom keybinding work allowing players to edit a file to customize mouse-and-keyboard controls to their liking.
Is it pretty? Nope. Does it work? Absolutely.
So, our first step is to allow players to customize via an .ini file while we continue to work on the implementation of in-game remapping for both mouse-and-keyboard and controller.
Fixed an issue that caused other Aces to slide around on the World Map.
Fixed an issue where the McKrakenstein and Iron Pox Masks names and descriptions were swapped in the Nightcloak’s Vault.
Combat: Fixed an issue that caused the Ace to ignore HitStop during attacks after being hit by an Environmental Hazard.

Combat: Fixed an issue where it was too easy to do infinite combos to airborne enemies with the Sentinel Class. You can still juggle enemies for quite awhile but they’ll eventually fall to the ground faster if you don’t mix up your combo enough.

Just to be clear, this isn’t the final solution. And, as soon as you get really good at this process - we encourage you to quickly forget it. Because, we’re going to put out a nice, shiny, user interface for remapping controls. Until then, you'll find a step-by-step instruction video below, with each step detailed beneath it. Enjoy remapping your controls!
Grab a Founder’s Pack - and Download Towerborne :)
Click on Towerborne in Steam so that the main game page is displayed with the Play button.
Click on the Manage button on the right side of the Play button.
Highlight Manage and select Browse Local Files. This will open the folder where Towerborne is installed.
Now that you’re in the Towerborne folder, double click on the Belfry folder.
While inside the Belfry folder, right click and select New -> Folder.
Name this folder “Config”.
Open the “Config” folder that you just created.
While inside the Config folder, right click and select New -> Text Document.
Name this document “UserInput.ini”.
You will get a confirmation message asking if you want to change the extension of the file.
Hit “Yes”.
If you don’t have Show File Extensions enabled, the above steps will not work. However, you can still create the .ini file by following similar steps.
1. Right Click -> Create New Text Document
2. Open the text document
3. Go to File -> Save As
4. Make sure the directory you're saving to is Towerborne -> Belfry -> Config
5. Under filename type “UserInput.ini” without quotations
6. In the Save as type select “All files”
This process should create the UserInput.ini file.
Double click on the new “UserInput.ini” file that you just created. This should open up your default text editing software.
Copy and Paste the following text into UserInput.ini. These are the game’s default controls.
[/Script/BfInput.BfEnhancedPlayerInput]
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Up",InputKeyName="W")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Down",InputKeyName="S")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Left",InputKeyName="A")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Right",InputKeyName="D")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Jump",InputKeyName="SpaceBar")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="LightAttack",InputKeyName="LeftMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="HeavyAttack",InputKeyName="RightMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Evade",InputKeyName="MiddleMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillShift",InputKeyName="LeftShift")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Umbra",InputKeyName="LeftControl")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="SocialWheel",InputKeyName="Three")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Interact",InputKeyName="E")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillLight",InputKeyName="X")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillHeavy",InputKeyName="C")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="ClassMechanic",InputKeyName="LeftAlt")
The InputMapName is largely self-explanatory. The Ace’s movement directions are Up, Down, Left, Right.
FocusSkillShift represents the modifier button for doing Focus Skills. If you hold this button and then press Light or Heavy Attack, you will do a Light or Heavy Focus Skill.

FocusSkillLight and FocusSkillHeavy provide alternative button mappings so that you can just press a single button to perform those specific actions. No need to even use the FocusSkillShift key. It’s not displayed anywhere in the game, but with default controls this is already assigned to X and C. It’s also assigned to I and O by default if you’re just using Keyboard Controls.
To change your controls, change the “InputKeyName” section to the Keybind of your choice.
For example, if you want Evade to be mapped to Left Shift, it would look like this:
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Evade",InputKeyName="LeftShift")
Once you’re done making your modifications, save the UserInput.ini file.

Now you’re ready to play the game! Once you load the game, your new control scheme should just work. Since these changes are being made in an .ini file, you cannot make changes while the game is running. Sorry.

It’s also worth noting that you will not see your new keys displayed in-game. This will work once the full feature is released, but for now the inputs you see on screen will not be reflective of your changes.
